findings.why_it_matters: Markdown heading depth is flattened erratically inside the 14.8 subtree, so 14.8.2.2 renders as a peer of 14.8 rather than a child of 14.8.2, and 14.8.2.3.3 (page 601, '## 14.8.2.3.3') renders as a peer of its own grandparent. Anything that builds a TOC or an outline from heading level - not from the clause number - nests these subclauses wrongly. No normative text is lost and the true depth is still recoverable from the printed clause number, which is why this is cosmetic rather than structural.
findings.suggested_repair: Normalize heading level to clause depth across the 14.8 subtree. Instances in this batch (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line numbers at time of check): 24963 '## 14.8.2.2', 24980 '## 14.8.2.3', 24983 '### 14.8.2.3.1', 24988 '### 14.8.2.3.2', 25055 '## 14.8.2.3.3', 25094 '## 14.8.3', 25180 '## 14.8.4', 25201 '## 14.8.4.3', 25210 '## 14.8.4.4', plus 23514-area precedents '## 14.7.7' (p594) and '## 14.7.8' (p596). NOTE: this is a global property of the transcription, not local to this batch - clause 14 itself is '## 14 Procedure division' while 14.8 is also '## 14.8', so a fix should be a document-wide normalization pass, not a per-page edit.
